questions.q: At the modification (rent cut, term unchanged, not a separate contract), Vertex remeasures the liability using:
o: Original 8% on old payments
Revised rent discounted at the revised discount rate at modification date, adjusting ROU by the same amount
Revised rent at 0%
No remeasurement until next year
questions.why: Ind AS 116: for a modification not accounted for as a separate contract, remeasure using the revised discount rate at the effective date of the change; the ROU is adjusted correspondingly.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).

questions.q: The effect of the remeasurement is:
o: Gain in P&L
ROU asset reduced by the same fall in liability, future interest recomputed
Lease terminated and a new one recognised
Liability unchanged
questions.why: Smaller future cash flows shrink the liability; no P&L for a rent-only reduction — the ROU absorbs it, then interest = new liability × new rate.

questions.q: Borrowings specifically taken for a qualifying asset were temporarily invested, earning Rs 4 crore investment income in the year. Under Ind AS 23, this income:
o: Is other income and never affects capitalisation
Reduces the amount of borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation
Is capitalised alongside interest
Creates negative borrowing cost and is ignored
questions.why: Ind AS 23 requires income earned on the temporary investment of specific borrowings to be DEDUCTED from the borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — specific-borrowing netting rule reappears in every second attempt AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Specific borrowing income nets against capitalised interest — general pool income does not. Follow the money's tag: 'for the asset' or not.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: A company is party to litigation. Counsel advises it is 'probable but not virtually certain' the court will award Rs 25 crore against it at year-end. Under Ind AS 37 the entity should:
o: Recognise a provision of Rs 25 crore
Disclose a contingent liability only
Do nothing — no outflow is possible
Recognise Rs 25 crore as a liability and ignore disclosure
questions.why: Probable (more likely than not) outflow that is reliably estimable ⇒ recognise a PROVISION. Only when the outflow is possible-but-not-probable is it a contingent liability (disclose); 'remote' ⇒ do nothing.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the three-way provision/disclose/nothing decision is the most-tested Ind AS 37 line Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Provision ladder: probable ⇒ book it; possible ⇒ disclose; remote ⇒ forget. Best estimate = weighted outcomes for a class, most-likely for single obligation.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: An unavoidable-cost situation arises when a rental contract (non-cancellable) cannot be cancelled and the entity no longer uses the space. Ind AS 37 measures the onerous-contract provision as:
o: Present value of net cash outflows expected — the LOWER of expected cost of performance and expected compensation/penalties for failure to perform
Gross rent for the entire term
The full contract value as an asset impairment
Zero — leases alone have their own recognition
questions.why: A provision for an onerous contract is the present value of the LOWER of (a) the net cost of performing the contract and (b) compensation/penalties for exiting it. Since the contract is non-cancellable here, performance cost typically governs.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 'lower of performance vs penalty' rule is a favourite discriminator AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Onerous = lower-of two exits, discounted. No walking away free, no double-counting.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: A lessee's lease payments include a residual value guarantee (RVG) of Rs 5 crore, of which the lessee expects to owe Rs 2 crore at the end. The lease liability includes:
o: The full Rs 5 crore RVG
Only the amount probable to be payable under the guarantee — Rs 2 crore
Zero — RVGs never enter the liability
Rs 5 crore discounted only in separate financials
questions.why: Ind AS 116: fixed payments include amounts expected to be payable by the lessee under residual value guarantees — the expected shortfall, not the whole guarantee.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — RVG inclusion basis is a precise-mechanics MCQ ICAI loves Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Guarantees enter the liability at their expected PAYABLE gap, not their face. Guarantee 5, expect owe 2, book 2.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: A lease of 11 months with an option to extend for another 6 months (not reasonably certain to exercise) and no purchase option qualifies for the lessee's short-term exemption because:
o: The term is 12 months or less at commencement and no purchase option
Any lease under a year is always short-term
It was signed at the start of the year
Rent was prepaid
questions.why: Short-term lease = 12 months or less at commencement AND no purchase option; unexercised optional periods excluded unless reasonably certain. Practical expedients are policy-by-class.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the '12 months AND no PO' conjunctive test is a favourite Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Short-term lease: ≤12 months + no purchase option. Miss either condition and the asset appears on your balance sheet anyway.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: Which correctly completes the matrix: present obligation (probable) / possible obligation / remote?
o: Provision / disclose / nothing
Provision / provision / disclose
Disclose / provision / nothing
Nothing / disclose / provision
questions.why: The Ind AS 37 decision grid — probable outflow: recognise; possible: disclose; remote: silence.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the grid is the most repeated pattern in Ch 7 Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Present+probable ⇒ provision; possible ⇒ note; remote ⇒ nothing. Three doors, one key each.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: A lessee cannot readily determine the rate implicit in the lease. The discount rate for measuring the lease liability is:
o: Government bond yield
The lessee's incremental borrowing rate
Prime lending rate
Coupon of the lease's residual guarantee
questions.why: Ind AS 116 requires the rate implicit in the lease if readily determinable, else the lessee's incremental borrowing rate.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — fallback-rate sequencing is a standard 1-marker AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Implicit rate first; IBR only as its understudy — never the lender's headline rate.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: A lessee obtains ownership of the underlying asset at the end of the lease term; the ROU asset should be depreciated:
o: Over the lease term
Up to the useful life of the underlying asset
For half the lease term
Not depreciated
questions.why: If ownership transfers (or purchase option reasonably certain to be exercised), depreciate to end of useful life; else shorter of lease term and useful life.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — ownership-transfer changes the clock Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Owning it eventually? Depreciate like an owner (life). Merely renting? The lease term caps the clock.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: A lessor grants a 3-month rent-free fit-out period. The lessee treats the incentive as:
o: Ignored
A reduction of lease payments in measuring the lease liability/ROU asset (incentives are deducted)
Other income
Prepaid expense of the full rent
questions.why: Lease incentives received (cash, rent-free periods, reimbursed costs) reduce the lease payments used to measure the liability/ROU.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the 'payments net of incentives' rule Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Free months aren't invisible: net them out of the payments — the liability shrinks too.
mem.link: Ch 7

questions.q: Which strongly indicates a finance lease?
o: Term is 50% of asset's economic life
Transfer of ownership at the end by bargain
Rent-free month at start
Lessor retains insurance
questions.why: Transfer of ownership (or bargain purchase option), lease term major part of economic life, PV ≈ substantially all FV — indicators of finance lease; 50% is not 'major part'.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — indicator-recognition with near-miss distractors AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Ownership ends where you? Finance. The 75% rule of thumb needs a 'major part' argument, not half.
mem.link: Chapter 7 — Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements

questions.q: In a selling-type lease, the lessor recognises manufacturing profit/loss at:
o: Year 1
Lease commencement, after removing the carrying cost of the asset
End of term
Rental receipts
questions.why: Finance lease (selling type) lessor books selling profit at commencement (FV/cash price − cost), plus a receivable; interest over time.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the timing-of-selling-profit rule AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The sale completes when the lease starts — collect the margin then, interest later.

questions.q: The lessor's net investment in a finance lease equals:
o: Gross lease payments
PV of lease payments + unguaranteed residual value (discounted at rate implicit in the lease)
Asset cost
Rent annualised
questions.why: Lessor: NILE = PV of lease payments (minimum + unguaranteed residual) at the implicit rate; the difference from cost = unearned finance income.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — residual-inclusive definition with the discount nuance AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Unguaranteed residual rides in the PV too — the lessor counts the whole expected stream.

questions.q: An intermediate lessee that subleases the same asset at FV references the:
o: Head-lease asset
Original lease's ROU asset (and its own lease classification test)
Lessor's book
Fair value of the underlying, always
questions.why: Sub-lease classification (finance vs operating for the intermediate lessor) uses the RIGHT-OF-USE asset from the head lease, not the underlying asset (short-term head lease exception: operating).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the ROU-swap is the exact trick AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The middleman leases his lease, not the landlord's building — classify off the ROU.

questions.q: Lessee's variable payments based on a sales threshold are included in lease payments when:
o: Index-based only
They are in-substance fixed (e.g., minimum guarantees that will inevitably be met)
All variable
Never
questions.why: Variable lease payments are included only when in-substance fixed; sales-based percentage rents are excluded until incurred.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — in-substance-fixed gate Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A promise with an escape clause is no promise yet — only the floor belongs to the liability.
mem.link: Chapter 7 — Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements

questions.q: Under the amendment to Ind AS 116 for sale-and-leaseback transactions, the seller-lessee's ROU asset from the leaseback is measured by reference to:
o: The full sale price
The carrying amount of the previous right of use transferred to the buyer (i.e., only the rights transferred generate gain/loss), with off-market terms adjusted
The FV of the asset in all cases
Zero
questions.why: Documented amendment (India: periods beginning on/after 1 April 2023): the seller-lessee recognises gain/loss only on the rights transferred to the buyer; where FV of consideration or the asset is off-market, the excess is treated as a prepayment (additional financing if below-market) — the 'no gain on my retained use' rule.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — SLB is the highest-yield arithmetic of the amendment cluster AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: You cannot sell the roof over your head and book a profit on the ceiling you kept — adjust the price to market first.
mem.link: Chapter 7 — Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements

questions.q: Sable Ltd enters a 6-year equipment lease on 1 April 20X1 with annual rentals of Rs 139 lakh payable in advance (from the commencement date), IBR 8%. Initial direct costs Rs 7 lakh. Rentals start one year later. The lease liability and ROU asset at commencement are (round to Rs lakh):
o: Liability Rs 623.54 lakh; ROU asset Rs 630.54 lakh
Liability Rs 623.54 lakh; ROU asset Rs 616.54 lakh
Liability Rs 841.00 lakh; ROU asset Rs 848.00 lakh
Liability Rs 623.54 lakh; ROU asset Rs 623.54 lakh
questions.why: PV of 6 rentals of Rs 139 lakh at 8% (factor 4.49) = Rs 623.54 lakh. ROU = liability + initial direct costs 7 = Rs 630.54 lakh. No discounting gives 841.00 (wrong); expensing IDC or equating ROU to the liability also misstates the asset.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — lease initial-measurement arithmetic is a fixture of Section B short sums Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Lease liability = PV of unpaid fixed payments at IBR (annuity-due when paid at year-start). ROU = liability + prepaid + initial direct costs − incentives.
mem.link: Chapter 7 — Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
